page: Amazon Web Services r8i.16xlarge is a memory-optimized server powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs and 32 physical cores from an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor operating at 3.9 GHz. The system includes a 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It is equipped with 512.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. This configuration does not include local storage or GPUs, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 30 Gbps.

Benchmark results show strong multi-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 69209.39 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 21093.0. The server demonstrates top-tier capabilities in software compilation with Clang and image processing. Memory performance is robust, showing a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 5123.16 GB/sec and a large block uncached read bandwidth of 192.43 GB/sec. For database operations, the server achieves a Passmark database score of 28496.57 and handles 120.37 million Redis SET operations per second. It also exhibits high static web serving throughput at 105.57 GB/sec.

The r8i.16xlarge is optimized for memory-intensive workloads, including large-scale databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, and data processing tasks. The inclusion of Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions supports medium-scale LLM inference, processing 7B model prompts at 296.71 tokens per second. However, the lack of local NVMe storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which may impact I/O-heavy workloads. The absence of a dedicated GPU also limits its utility for heavy deep learning training, though CPU-based inference remains viable.
